images.title: Midpoints make 4 identical triangles
images.purpose: Shows that joining the midpoints of an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm cuts it into 4 identical equilateral triangles of side 4 cm.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. One large equilateral triangle, point up, divided by the three lines that join its midpoints.
images.exact_structure: One large equilateral triangle, point up, side 8 units, thin dark outline. The midpoint of each of its 3 sides is marked with a small reddish purple #CC79A7 dot: 3 dots. The 3 midpoints are joined by 3 thin dark straight lines, making 4 small equilateral triangles of exactly equal size: 3 corner triangles (top, bottom left, bottom right) filled teal #0072B2 and 1 upside down middle triangle filled amber #E69F00. Labels: below the base, a thin grey bracket spanning the whole base with '8 cm' under it; just above the base, '4 cm' on the left half of the base and '4 cm' on the right half; '4 cm' on the top (horizontal) side of the middle triangle, inside the amber; '60°' just inside the top corner of the big triangle. So '4 cm' appears 3 times, '8 cm' once, '60°' once. Nothing else.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Joining the midpoints makes 4 identical equilateral triangles, each with side 4 cm.
images.description: Shows that joining the midpoints of an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm cuts it into 4 identical equilateral triangles of side 4 cm.
images.context: Concept T3.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Corner triangle: two sides 4 cm with 60° between, base angles (180° − 60°) ÷ 2 = 60°, so all sides 4 cm.

image_decisions.why: The claim is about a shape cut into equal parts; the picture with the half lengths makes it visible at once.
